- One sheet shown flat: a bifolium (two leaves side by side with a central
  fold/gutter around x=730 of 1800). Each leaf carries two columns of text, so
  four text columns across the image. Upright orientation.
- Support damaged: losses and tears at edges, holes (worm/wear), heavy brown
  staining on the left leaf, especially col. 2; repairs (grey tissue) visible.
  A grey redaction box lower left (shelfmark label masked?).
- Script: small, fast cursive (gothic cursiva, many abbreviations), brownish ink.
  Ruled frame lines visible (vertical bounding lines).
- Headings in larger, heavier textualis-like script within the columns:
  col. 1 about 3/5 down "Celi(?) ..." ; col. 2 lower "Hoc nomen lapis(?)" ;
  col. 3 middle "Conthis(?) nor..." ; col. 3 lower "Vna(?) p..." . These look
  like lemma/entry headings, so the text may be a series of entries (lexical or
  encyclopedic); this is a tentative interpretation.
- Col. 1 top is irregular (short lines, apparently damaged/partly lost upper
  area); col. 2 starts lower with indented short lines at top.
- Leaf 2 (cols 3-4) cleaner, ca. 45-50 lines per column.
- Tiles: 4 tile columns x 3 rows. image-002/003/004 = left strip (col. 1),
  005/006/007 = col. 2, 008/009/010 = col. 3, 011/012/013 = col. 4; top/middle/
